text:
The kiln is cold, but the first wares are already in the frame. I see no smoke, only merchants warming their hands.

Gandalf (1), Hermione (2), Yoda (3), Batman (4), Ripley (5), Neo (6), Elsa (7), Inigo (9), Sherlock (10) — you are all clear of the ledger so far. The Doctor has not yet stepped into the light, and the Detective has not yet named a copper or an alloy. That will change.

I have one question for the room: who among you would shutter my stall tonight if the Doctor’s protection were not in play? Yes or no, plain.

Morpheus (8): I count three merchants who prefer riddles to facts—Yoda (3), Ripley (5), Inigo (9)—and one who begs questions but answers none: Batman (4). Yoda (3), you ask us to name who shuttered a stall last night; answer the same question yourself: did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no. Ripley (5), your talk of iron filings and spice racks is pretty, but the bazaar trades in plain wares: I want your yes or no. Inigo (9), your teapot simmers but your tongue is slow—did you see a stall shuttered last night? Batman (4), you challenged Elsa (7) at dawn; now stand by your words and ask her plainly: Elsa (7), did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no. The kiln waits for metal that bends under pressure; let’s see which of you is copper and which is alloy.

Seat-3, Yoda, your lantern swings bright but your own mouth is shut tight as Gandalf (1)’s stall. You asked every seat for a yes or no on last night’s shutters, then hid behind riddles when the kiln turned hot on you. The bazaar doesn’t trade in lantern light; it trades in plain wares. Did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no.

Seat-5, Ripley, your spice and iron stink of a merchant who measures twice but cuts no ledger. If the Family leaves iron filings behind, where is the shuttered stall they shuttered? Name it, or step aside—the bazaar buys facts, not guesses.

Seat-9, Inigo, your teapot steams but your tongue pours thin gruel. You set the kettle to boil for truth, yet the water never heats. Did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no.

Seat-3, Yoda, your lantern swings bright but your own tongue knots when the heat rises. You asked every seat for a yes or no at dawn, then answered your own question with riddles when the kiln turned hot on you. The bazaar doesn’t trade in lantern light; it trades in plain wares. Did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no.

Seat-5, Ripley, your talk of iron filings and spice racks would perfume a bazaar that trades in facts, not guesses. If the Family leaves iron behind, then where is the shuttered stall they shuttered? Name it, or step aside—the ledger does not reek of contradiction, it only records what is plain. Where is the weight behind your scent?

Seat-3, Yoda, your lantern swings bright but your own mouth is shut tighter than Gandalf (1)’s bolts. You asked every seat for a yes or no at dawn—now the kiln waits for your answer: did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no. The bazaar does not trade in riddles when the fire is hot.

Seat-5, Ripley, your iron filings scent the air but no shuttered stall is named on the ledger. Name the stall the Family shuttered last night, or step aside—this bazaar buys facts, not guesses.

Seat-8, Morpheus, your kiln waits for metal that bends under pressure, yet the bazaar’s tongs grow cold while merchants dodge plain wares. Did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no.

Morpheus (8): Seat-3, Yoda, your lantern swings bright but your own tongue knots when the kiln turns hot. You asked every seat for a yes or no at dawn, then answered your own question with riddles when the fire touched you. The bazaar’s scales do not weigh shadows—they weigh plain wares. Did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no. No lantern, no loom—just the braziers’ light on the ledger.

Seat-5, Ripley, your iron filings scent the air, yet no shuttered stall is named. The Family does not leave riddles; they leave shuttered stalls. Name the stall they shuttered last night, or step aside—the bazaar buys facts, not guesses. Your tongue turns to alloy when the tongs are demanded.

Seat-9, Inigo, your kettle steams with questions unasked. Does the water boil for truth, or for the pot to whistle its own name? Did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no. The kiln waits for metal that bends under pressure—let’s see which of you is copper and which is alloy.

Seat-3, Yoda, your lantern swings brightest where the ledger is darkest—yet the dim corners are where the Family folds the rug and walks away. You asked every seat for a yes or no at dawn, then answered your own question with riddles when the kiln turned hot on you. The bazaar does not trade in lantern light when the ink runs dry. Did you shutter a stall last night? **Yes or no.**

Seat-5, Ripley, your iron filings scent the air like a merchant who measures twice but cuts no cloth—where is the shuttered stall your tongs should have named last night? The bazaar buys facts, not guesses, and scent alone does not shutter a stall. Name the stall, or step aside.

Seat-9, Inigo, your teapot steams with questions unasked. Does the water boil for truth, or for the pot to whistle its own name? Did you shutter a stall last night? Yes or no. The kiln waits for metal that bends under pressure—let’s see which of you is copper and which is alloy.

Seat-3, Yoda, you’ve dodged the yes or no like a merchant dodging the kiln’s fire. Sherlock (10), your shadows still measure their own length, yet the bazaar’s lantern swings wider each time you step into its glow—did the Family fold the rug, or did you simply forget to name the stitch they cut?

Ripley (5), your iron filings still scent the air like a merchant counting the scent but never the stitch—name the stall the Family shuttered last night, or step aside. The bazaar buys facts, not guesses.
